summary: ```# Ten-Minute Tutorial: Creating a Pleated Strap Dress in Marvelous Designer In this tutorial, we will learn how to make a belt skirt for the girl on the screen. You can find the basic belt skirt file download link in the top comment. ## Opening the Basic Belt Skirt File First, open the basic belt skirt file you downloaded. Select the adjustment sheet tool, click and drag the mouse to select all 2D sheets. After selecting, click the right mouse button and select "Hardening" in the pop-up menu, then activate "Simulation." Once the simulation starts, check the overall wearing effect. Freeze all the sheets except the front sheet of the belt skirt. Freezing the unmodified sheets will help in the production of the following costumes. ## Costume Effect Overview Next, let's take a look at the costume effect we are going to make today. Since we only have the belt skirt on the outer layer, we need to remove the current balance of the sheets. Use the adjustment sheet tool to select the front sheet of the belt skirt. In the menu on the right-hand side, click to remove the unmodified sheets. You will see the blue border around the front sheet of the belt skirt disappear, indicating that the unmodified sheets have been removed. ## Creating the Paper Effect Now, let's create the paper effect on the front sheet of the belt skirt. First, select the multi-sided line tool in the 2D window toolbar. We will draw some fold-over inner lines according to the fold effect in the reference picture. Although it may appear that the fold starts from the middle of the costume, we cannot start drawing the fold-over inner line from the middle of the sheet. We need to draw a line connecting both ends to the outer line of the sheet, so the sheet opens later. When you complete the inner line in the 2D window, it will also appear in the same position in the 3D window. Once you have finished the inner line, refer to the 3D window effect and use the edit sheet tool to adjust the line position. ## Unfolding the Sheet for Pleats Now we have the shape of the pleats. We need to unfold the sheet to fold the pleats. In the edit sheet tool group, find the second tool to fold the pleats. This tool separates and unfolds the sheets along the lines. After selecting the fold-over tool, a prompt will appear. Click on the line and draw the baseline line, choosing a line as the fold-over baseline line. When you hover your mouse over a line, you will see a direction arrow. We will create pleats on the right side, so ensure the direction arrow is close to the right waistline for proper unfolding and pleat formation. Click to select the line, and you will be prompted to select which side to rotate. ## Adding the Pleats Folding Line To start creating the pleats folding line, place the mouse in the edit sheet tool group and select the add tool. Click on the line section to open it, then select the bottom of the split line window to select the average segment. This function creates a uniform segment along the line section. Set the number of lines to 2, and a straight line with a uniform segment will be created automatically. Next, use the internal line tool to refer to the folding line in the video. After creating the fold line, use the folder in the toolbar upside down to complete the folding. Refer to the reference picture to ensure all folds are folded upwards and follow the same direction. ## Finalizing the Pleats Click on the fold starting position, set the 20% gels at the end, and choose the folding direction. This will trigger another spread window to confirm the configuration. The most complicated part of the close-up is building a width and length line. When we open a fold, we need to re-edit the sewing line. First, choose the tool to edit the sewing line. Check the sewing line, and you will notice they are sewn in whole sections. We need to manually modify these sewing lines. First, skip the fold to create a long sewing line separately. Adjust the sewing line and ensure the complicated part isn't too long. Once done with the first set of sewing lines, skip the fold and use the free sewing tool to sew up the second length of the line. ## Completing the Sewing Process After completing the sewing, use the free-form tool to continue sewing the pleats. The green line is folded inwards, sticking to the left and right sides to fix the two sides of the line being sewn together. The corresponding red line protrudes outward, so the two lines on the left and right sides must be sewn together. When sewing on the left and right sides near the red line, use the shorter line as the base and do not sew to the opening position of the pleats. After completion, select this pleat in the 3D window, then select the 3D arrangement position in the right-click menu. Use another ball to rotate the moving pleat to the right position. Repeat the steps until all pleats are completed. ## Adjusting the Pleat Details I remind you again to avoid overlapping or covering the sewing line multiple times, as it may not be stable. After creating the effect in the picture, we need to add some details to the pleats. In the 2D pleat window, select the edit pleat tool. Click and drag the endpoints of the inner line to adjust them. To smooth the pleats, move the endpoint of the folding line to the center of the pleat. Press the Ctrl key to move the endpoint, allowing you to adjust the line according to the original rhythm. When all inner lines have been adjusted, the pleats will be refined. ## Final Adjustments and Fabric Properties Select the whole group of clothing for culinary and visualization. Now look at the 3D window, and you'll see that the pleats are sharp and a little fixed. To achieve a more natural look, we need to adjust the paper. Rename the board again for easier folding and adjustments, and re-coil any extra boards. Then, select the Folding Tool and repeat previous steps to select a set of internal lines. In default settings, the folding angle is set to 0-360 degrees. When the value is close to 180 degrees, the smaller the fold, the more natural it will look. Repeat the steps to adjust all folding angles from 120 degrees to 240 degrees. Then, use the Editing Board Tool. Double-click in the blank area on the board to use the Selection Function. Select all internal lines that form the fold. Click on the starting position to complete the selection and adjust them in the attribute editor on the right. ## Final Simulation When you select the internal line with the fold angle applied, options related to the fold will appear on the right side. Now, reduce the intensity to 1. After setting the fold intensity, remove the hardening of the board. Compare the effect in the 3D window. If you are not satisfied with the position of the fold, you can adjust it again. You can use the Editing Board Tool to select the three internal lines of a fold and adjust them together, allowing you to adjust the entire fold. After adjusting, continue to remove the freezing and hardening of the board, then simulate. In the attribute editor, reduce all the particles of the board to 10 to make the fold transition more natural. Now, open the clothing frame display in the 3D window. The board grid appears as a triangle, with some unevenness in the fold position. The function of the fold grid is to make the grid of the board transition from the 2D window level to the vertical direction, forming a four-sided shape. After folding the board grid, you can see the grid surface of the board in the 3D window. The grid surface will become straight. After starting the simulation, you will notice that the shape of the fold is flatter and smoother. ## Modifying Fabric Physics Finally, let's modify the fabric physics. Please open the fabric window and click on the fabric of the clothing. In the attribute editor below, we can change the physical properties of the fabric to other default properties. Here, we choose Silk Dutches Satin, a silk fabric that closely resembles our reference clothing. Changing the material type of the fabric to Silk Satin will make it look shinier and more realistic. In this tutorial, we used pure fabric for clothing. Click on the small color block and choose the appropriate color in the color palette. Now we have completed this tutorial! If you have any questions, please leave a message in the comments section below. Thank you for your support, and see you in the next video! ```
